claims.text: HRW: 1,195 people were killed in the 7 October assault, 815 of them civilians by AFP's cross-referencing; armed groups took 251 civilians and security personnel to Gaza; the Qassam Brigades led the assault with at least four other armed groups; at least 19 kibbutzim, 5 moshavim, Sderot and Ofakim, two music festivals and a beach party were attacked.

HRW concluded that 'the planned murder of civilians and the hostage-taking were crimes against humanity', that killing civilians and taking hostages were 'central aims of the planned attack', and listed war crimes including willful killing, cruel treatment, mutilation of bodies and crimes involving sexual and gender-based violence; Hamas authorities said fighters were instructed not to target civilians.

At the Nova festival the IDF's April 2025 investigation counted 378 killed (344 civilians, 34 security personnel), revising an earlier 364; 44 were taken hostage; a police officer's decision at 6:35 a.m. to shut the event is credited with saving hundreds.

In Be'eri, a community of about 1,000, 101 civilians and 31 security personnel were killed and 30 residents and two other civilians taken hostage; at Pessi Cohen's house a tank fired shells on the order of Brig. Gen. Barak Hiram and 13 of the 14 Israelis held there were found dead; large Israeli forces entered the kibbutz only around 6 p.m.
The IDF inquiry found Hamas used more than 60 attack routes where planners expected at most eight border points; about 1,200 were killed and 251 taken hostage.

Hagari (11 Jul 2024): 'The IDF failed in its mission to protect the residents of Kibbutz Be'eri'; the inquiry found 'no civilians inside the building were hit by tank fire', 'most of the hostages inside the house were murdered by the terrorists', hostages outside were hit by tank shrapnel and it is 'highly likely that one of them was killed as a result'; tank fire came after negotiations were exhausted; 'a developing inquiry'.
The probe judged Hiram's order 'reasonable in view of the conditions'; kibbutz members said it 'failed to answer critical questions' and called for a state-level panel.

claims.text: Israeli officials obtained an approximately 40-page Hamas attack plan code-named 'Jericho Wall' more than a year before 7 October; it called for rocket barrages, drones to disable cameras and machine guns, and gunmen on paragliders, motorcycles and foot; officials dismissed it as 'aspirational'; in July 2023 a Unit 8200 analyst wrote 'I utterly refute that the scenario is imaginary' and a Gaza division colonel replied 'let's wait patiently'.

The IDF's inquiry (27 Feb 2025) found Israel 'underestimated its capabilities' and wrongly believed Hamas 'was more interested in governing the territory than fighting Israel'; Chief of Staff Herzi Halevi said 'I was the commander of the military on October 7th, and I have my own responsibility' and resigned; Netanyahu resisted calls for a commission of inquiry.

As of October 2026 no state commission of inquiry had been established; the government told the Supreme Court in summer 2025 it did not intend to establish one; Netanyahu prefers a commission with equal coalition and opposition representation and rejected President Herzog's compromise; a bill passed first reading in July 2026 but was not completed before the Knesset dissolved; a State Comptroller examination exists.

entries.topic: The accounts: Hamas, the inquiries, Hannibal, and the first response

claims.text: Hamas's 16-page 'Our Narrative' (21 Jan 2024) called the attack 'a necessary step and a normal response to confront all Israeli conspiracies against the Palestinian people', cited prisoners, settlements and the 'Judaization' of the West Bank and Jerusalem, said fighters 'only targeted Israeli soldiers and people carrying weapons', said 'maybe some faults happened' due to 'the rapid collapse of the Israeli security and military system'.

The UN mission led by Pramila Patten (report 4 March 2024) found 'reasonable grounds to believe' conflict-related sexual violence including rape and gang rape occurred on 7 October, including on Road 232 and at Kibbutz Re'im, and 'clear and convincing information' that some hostages were subjected to sexual violence; it found at least two widely repeated Be'eri allegations 'unfounded', could not meet any victims, and said a fully-fledged investigation was needed; Hamas denied the allegations.

Haaretz reported (7 July 2024) that IDF commands invoked the Hannibal procedure, officially repealed in 2016, on 7 October: 'Hannibal at Erez' with an attack drone, similar orders at Re'im camp and Nahal Oz, and an instruction that 'not a single vehicle could return to Gaza'; a Southern Command source said 'you couldn't really know if there were any such people in a vehicle'.
On 9 October 2023 Defence Minister Yoav Gallant said 'We are putting a complete siege on Gaza … No electricity, no food, no water, no gas – it's all closed.'
An Israeli Air Force probe found Efrat Katz of Nir Oz was likely killed by helicopter fire.
An army official said friendly-fire incidents occurred but 'there were not many', without a figure.
Hamas's 'Our Narrative' said many Israelis 'were killed by the Israeli army and police due to their confusion'.
